title: mov & registers
description:
The two most important concepts of assembly are mov and registers. `mov` stores data in registers, but to understand `mov` you must know what registers are.

---
Registers store data. There are 16 general purpose registers in X86-64 ASM, rax, rbx, rcx, rdx, rsi, rdi, rbp, rsp and r8, r9, r10, r11, r12, r13, r14, r15. There are many other registers, but the 2 most important ones are `rax`, and `rdi`. `rax` is for storing what command you want to run, and `rdi` is for storing the first value of a syscall.
`mov` is simple in comparison. `mov` is used to move data into registers, with syntax `mov register, value`
## Assignment:
Replace the comment (starts with ;) with some register tests, then click the registers tab, and you can view your registers, then answer the question.
